title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 68
paragraphs: This proclamation, I say, he made as soon as he established himself on the throne. But in the eighth month his identity was discovered, and it came about in this way. There was a certain Otanes son of Pharnaspes, inferior to no Persian in birth or wealth. This Otanes was the first to suspect that the Magian was not Smerdis son of Cyrus but the person he really was, drawing his inference from these facts: that he never went out of the fortress, and that he did not summon any of the distinguished men among the Persians into his presence. Having formed this suspicion, he proceeded as follows. Cambyses had married Otanes' daughter, whose name was Phaidyme; and this same daughter the Magian was now keeping as his wife, living with her as with all the other wives of Cambyses. So Otanes sent a message to this daughter, asking who the man was beside whom she slept—whether Smerdis son of Cyrus or some other. She sent back word that she did not know, for she had never seen Smerdis son of Cyrus, nor did she know otherwise who the man was who lived with her. Otanes then sent a second time and said: “If you yourself do not know Smerdis son of Cyrus, then ask Atossa who this man is with whom both she and you live as wives. For she must surely know her own brother.”
